findings.title: Zero VectorType panics on nil-pointer deref for *any destination
findings.claim: The new Dimensions > 0 guard prevents the bound check from dereferencing a nil SubType, but info.Zero() (via marshal.go:2046, v.SubType.NewWithError()) still panics; `var dst any; Unmarshal(VectorType{}, []byte{}, &dst)` panics with a nil-pointer dereference, verified by running it. The new test pins this input shape only for *[]float64, so it passes while the interface-destination case still crashes.

findings.title: Nested vector's inner type keeps bare VectorType name, breaking parsing
findings.claim: The PR teaches the basic-type branch to preserve the server's name but this branch still stores prefix+"VectorType" without the parenthesized subtype, so asVectorType cannot parse it, NewWithError fails, Zero() returns nil, and a nested-vector column errors out of MapScan/Scan(&any) with an unhelpful message. Passing name here would fix it; the PR defers this to #1085.

findings.title: VectorType.Zero() discards the NewWithError error, losing failure reason
findings.claim: VectorType.Zero() discards the error returned by NewWithError, so the new error message at marshal.go:1048 can only name the type and not the reason for the failure.

findings.title: Non-NULL zero-length payload for Dimensions > 0 now errors instead of decoding to zero values
findings.claim: The documented behavior change is correct but is a visible API break for anyone who relied on a non-NULL zero-length payload with Dimensions > 0 decoding to zero values instead of erroring.
